text:
**Short answer:** 30W is the minimum to charge a MacBook Air, and 65-70W gets you fast charging. Apple's own recommendations depend on the model (all from [Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-us/109509)):

- **2022 or later (M2, M3, M4, M5):** Apple lists the 30W (13-inch only), 35W Dual USB-C, 67W, and 70W adapters. The M5 13-inch ships with a 40W Dynamic Power Adapter (60W max). The M4 13-inch ships with either a 30W or 35W adapter, depending on GPU configuration ([M4 specs](https://fd.xuwubk.eu.org/https/support.apple.com/en-us/122209), [M5 specs](https://fd.xuwubk.eu.org/https/support.apple.com/en-us/126320)).
- **2018-2021 (Intel and M1):** Apple 30W, or the 40W Dynamic adapter (60W max).

**Fast charging:** Apple says fast charging needs a **70W or higher** USB PD source on the recent models. Apple's pages don't give a rule for 65W chargers, so I'd go with 70W if fast charging matters.

**Third-party chargers:** Apple says any USB-C charger that supports USB Power Delivery will work, even at higher or lower wattage than recommended. For the best experience, match at least the wattage Apple recommends for your model.

**Checking what you have:** Hold Option, click the Apple menu, choose System Information, then Power. The wattage is listed under AC Charger Information.

**If you want a third-party option:** The [Baseus GaN5 Pro 65W 2-pack](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-gan5-pro-65w-2c-u) is $49.99 and gives 65W from a single USB-C port. If you plug in more devices, the laptop port drops to 45W, which still charges a MacBook Air but not at fast-charge speed. Note that this is an affiliate link, and the retailer-page source says Dealectric is paid if you buy. It's a 65W unit, so it falls short of Apple's 70W fast-charge threshold. The 100W [ESR 6-in-1 station](https://dealectric.com/go/esr-100w-6-in-1-magsafe-cryoboost-station) works too, but at $164.99 (or $135.30 with code PARTNER18) it's more than a MacBook Air needs unless you want the MagSafe and Apple Watch pads.

If you tell me which year and size of MacBook Air you have, I can narrow it down further.
